label: copy phase: input k while outputting u (k->u transition)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input is a repeated token (in_first=0). Almost always the input is k (94% of mass); the rest is input u. It fires most strongly when the fed-back input is k and the token being output is u, i.e. the original sequence had the bigram k u. That case covers 76% of activation mass and over 90% of the top quartile. The top examples (around 3.0) are k->u at recall_idx 2-4, near the end of the sequence (to_go 0-1). Weaker activations come from k followed by other outputs (w, p, d, 2, k) and from u->u repeats. Never fires in the original or delimiter phases, at recall_idx 0-1, or on any other input token. k->u early in a long sequence, with many outputs still to go, is often silent; most false positives are of that kind. Dev F1 is 0.62 (P 0.69, R 0.56).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=k (+7.11), phase=2 & in_tok=u (+5.86), phase=2 & out_tok=u (+4.33), out_tok=u (+4.06), next_out=u (+3.96), in_tok=k (+3.15). Lower it: recall_idx=1 (-3.46), prev_tok=<DEL> (-3.46), orig_idx=-1 (-2.92), orig4=c (-2.09).
